svg.text: From a haplotype sheet to outbreak clusters
Every step below is in PyEuk's compute_revised_wibs_matrix() and find_clusters(). Read processing is upstream of this and is not shown.
Step 1: quality filter, encoding, locus grouping
locus_mask
rows = specimens, columns = named haplotypes, X = detected
X = (values == "X") - the sheet holds only X and empty
depth and frequency are not lost here: they are not in the sheet at all,
and the column names index haplotypes78.fa, so sequence is unused not lost
column name cut at _Hap_ gives the locus: 165 columns -> 25 loci
a locus block with at least one X was typed; an empty block was not
specimens with X in under 10% of columns are dropped - 9 of 153 here
Step 2: allele weighting
w_j
p_j = mean(X[called, j]), w_j = 1 / sqrt(p_j (1 - p_j))
frequency is taken over specimens where the locus was called
rare columns weigh more - see panel at right
Step 3: pairwise distance
_fast_numba_wibs
d(i,j) = SUM w_k |x_ik - x_jk| / SUM w_k
the sum runs only over loci called in BOTH specimens
a locus one of them dropped contributes nothing either way
Step 4: Euclidean repair
np.linalg.eigh
G = -1/2 H D^2 H, eigh, clip negatives, back to distances
Ward's method assumes the distances are drawable as points
without this step they are not
Step 5: Ward linkage
scipy.linkage
every specimen starts in its own cluster
each merge is the one that costs least in added spread
cost = (|A||B| / (|A|+|B|)) x d(centre A, centre B)^2
Step 6: tree cut
find_clusters
cut at the largest relative gap between merge heights
three guards decide whether to cut at all - see panel at right
if none is met the answer is one cluster
What an empty cell means
Three locus windows, five specimens.
locus 1
locus 2
locus 3
S1
S2
S3
S4
S5
detected
not detected, locus was typed
locus not typed
S1 and S2 are compared over loci 1 and 3 only.
Scoring S2's blank locus-2 block as five absences would
make a sequencing failure look like a different genotype.
Why rare columns weigh more
w = 1 / sqrt(p (1 - p)), the standard deviation of a coin flip, inverted.
w
p, the fraction of typed specimens carrying that haplotype
A haplotype in 5% of specimens counts 2.3x one in 50%. A column that is rare
because its locus keeps failing gets exactly the same promotion.
Why the eigenvalues get clipped
Positive semi-definite means the distances can be drawn as points on a map.
negative eigenvalues
set to zero
Before this projection was added, the delivered matrix had lambda_min = -1.9453,
with 152 of its 153 eigenvalues negative.
Where the tree gets cut
The largest relative gap between consecutive merge heights.
cut
gap
Three guards decide whether that cut is reported:
1. the gap rule is searched from k = 2 upward, never k = 1
2. the gap must be >= 22% of the total tree height
3. the smallest cluster must reach max(5, 10% of N)
If no candidate clears all three, the answer is one cluster.
Measured on the 2018 CDC benchmark — 153 specimens with CDC haplotype calls, labelled by two epidemiologically-defined outbreaks.
Label-free, this path returns k = 2 with ARI 0.9721. Its distance separates same-outbreak from different-outbreak pairs at AUC 0.7692,
against 0.9964 for CDC's legacy heuristic distance on the same specimens. The clustering layer is not the limiting step.

The locus-typed rule in Step 1, the shared-loci restriction in Step 3 and the Euclidean repair in Step 4 were added in response to public review. The numbers above are from the state after those changes.
